sanskrit_verse: चतुष्पादकृतो दोषो नापेहीति प्रजल्पतः / काष्ठलोष्टेषुपाषाणबाहुयुग्यकृतस् तथा //
transliteration: catuṣpādakṛto doṣo nāpehīti prajalpataḥ / kāṣṭhaloṣṭeṣupāṣāṇabāhuyugyakṛtas tathā //
sph_interpretive_translation: Fault arising from four-footed beings, or from mere talk without action, or caused by wood, clods, stones, or bodily contact—such faults do not incur liability under Dharma.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates solely in conscious intent aligned with SPH's Dharma
Causation is valid only when rooted in volitional capacity, not passive interaction
Capacity-based responsibility excludes inert or non-intentional agents
Restoration logic applies exclusively where conscious agency initiates disruption
Consciousness alignment determines the validity of any juridical consequence
executable_legal_axioms: IF action originates from non-volitional entity THEN no dharma-liability arises
IF causal agent lacks conscious intent THEN exclusion from restorative process
IF fault results from inert materials OR animal motion THEN nullify legal consequence
IF speech is unaccompanied by actionable embodiment THEN treat as non-event
IF actor's awareness-level is below sentient threshold THEN defer to consciousness-realignment protocol
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this axiom establishes a threshold of intentional agency. Cases involving mechanical failure, animal behavior, or idle speech must be dismissed unless conscious misalignment is demonstrable. The court must recognize that only volitional acts rooted in human or divine intelligence qualify for dharma-based inquiry.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality demands proof of intentional initiation. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that inert objects and involuntary utterances lack sequential moral force. Proportional responsibility aligns with the actor's capacity for conscious choice. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that absence of will negates juridical consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process only upon verification of sentient involvement
Realign consciousness of affected parties through śuddhi-darśana protocols
Restore systemic integrity via dharmic resonance assessment
Ensure no punitive attribution to non-agent entities
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. Fault without volition is void in law. Justice serves restoration alone. Consciousness is the ultimate adjudicator. Dharma stands reaffirmed.
